newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products knocked lower by crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products knocked lower by crude.

text.p: Med oil products were steady to weaker, knocked lower by falling crude.
Gasoline prices were weaker in line with falling NYMEX futures but the region remains relatively tight.

High sulphur fuel oil was better bid and numbers were looking healthier. A trader was heard to have won a 75,000 tonne Romanian tender, for early March delivery, and was thought likely to fill it with transatlantic barrels.
A Turkish tender was announced to sell 45-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil, to load in Aliaga on March 7-9. The tender closes on Tuesday.
A refiner was heard to be seeking some bunker product to cover requirements in Gibraltar and the Canaries.
Low sulphur fuel oil was sharply weaker alongside crude. The market remains long, although a little new refiner interest is seen into Italy and Lavera.

Naphtha lost about $2 a tonne to hover around $204-205 fob Med reflecting sharp losses on crude. Traders said activity was very slow, with local demand poor and numerous players still out of the market.

Gas oil was weakened by a $2.50 drop on futures although premiums were holding. Traders saw Russian material around cif high quotes flat while diesel prices were unchanged supported from continued buying interest from South America.
